intended_object: The descent (factorization) of a (semi)linear map g : M → P through a surjective (semi)linear map f : M → N when ker f ≤ ker g. This is the unique linear map ḡ : N → P with ḡ ∘ f = g, i.e. the universal property of the quotient N ≅ M / ker f. I took this from the docstring and the companion lemmas `liftOfSurjective_apply` and `liftOfSurjective_comp`.
explanation:
The underlying function is `Function.extend f g 0`. Because f is surjective, the value 0 off the range of f is never used, so this function is well defined and equals g(x) at f(x). The condition ker f ≤ ker g gives `FactorsThrough g f`: f x = f y implies x − y ∈ ker f ⊆ ker g, so g x = g y. This step uses subtraction, which is why M must be an additive group. The additivity and semilinearity proofs pick preimages under f and under σ, and σ is assumed surjective (`RingHomSurjective σ`). Together with `RingHomCompTriple σ τ ρ`, this is exactly what is needed for the descended map to be τ-semilinear.

The generality is natural. Arbitrary semirings with ring homomorphisms σ, ρ, τ cover the plain linear case and more. N and P only need to be additive commutative monoids. Requiring M to be an additive group is the right setting: over a monoid, a kernel condition does not imply factorization in general.

Mathlib has `RingHom.liftOfSurjective`, `MonoidHom.liftOfSurjective`, `AlgHom.liftOfSurjective` and `Derivation.liftOfSurjective`, but no `LinearMap.liftOfSurjective`. For linear maps the same result can only be obtained by combining `Submodule.liftQ` with `LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective`, so no single Mathlib declaration matches. The definition is correct and stated at its natural generality.
